title: What if you were 10 times taller?
caption:
Giant-sized, your legs would snap. 🦴📏

Scale a 1.75 m, 70 kg adult up ten times in every direction: 17.5 m tall, and about 70 tonnes (×1,000).

But a bone's strength depends on its cross-section, which grows only ×100. So every bone carries ten times the stress.

Running already loads leg bones to about 55 MPa, with a safety margin of only about 3–4× before they fail. Ten times that, and one run breaks them. Biologist J.B.S. Haldane made this point in 1926.

The only fix: let water carry the weight. That's how blue whales get so big.

Send this to the tallest friend you have.

A new impossible experiment every day.

⚠️ Don't try this. Don't test your bones with jumps or heavy loads: overloaded bones fracture.

#science #physics #whatif #sciencefacts #squarecubelaw #biology #giants #theimpossiblelab
sources: https://www.marxists.org/archive/haldane/works/1920s/right-size.htm (J.B.S. Haldane, On Being the Right Size, 1926: giants 10× as high, wide and thick weigh 1,000×, bone cross-sections only 100×, each square inch of bone carries 10× the weight; the human thigh-bone breaks under about 10× body weight, so they would break their thighs at every step)

https://biewenerlab.oeb.harvard.edu/publications/musculoskeletal-design-relation-body-size (Biewener, Musculoskeletal design in relation to body size, J Biomech 1991: peak compressive bone stresses during locomotion −40 to −80 MPa, mean −55 ± 23 MPa; safety factor to compressive failure about 3–4)

https://www.discoverwildlife.com/animal-facts/marine-animals/why-are-marine-animals-so-big (water provides buoyancy that supports massive body weights, so marine animals don't need thick, heavy bones like land animals)
Computed: ×10 length → area ×100, volume and mass ×1,000; 70 kg → 70 t; 1.75 m → 17.5 m; stress = weight/area → ×10; 55 MPa × 10 = 550 MPa vs failure ≈ 55 × 3–4 = 165–220 MPa (≈200)
